v0.20.1 — exact amounts, memos and offline signing; a syncing node keeps what its transactions did

**Same chain, no coordinated update.** Replace the binary and restart; your data stays. Nothing in
this release changes consensus, the chain state or what nodes say to each other, so 0.20.0 and
0.20.1 nodes run side by side.

**Operators: update, especially before your node catches up again.** 0.20.0 threw away the outcome
of every transaction in a block it took over sync — all of them on joining, after every restart,
and now and then while following the chain. For those transactions it answered `unknown`, failed
ones included (#259). Blocks your node already synced keep that gap; it concerns only what your
node reports, never balances or consensus. Every block from 0.20.1 on is recorded.

**Wallets and CLI**

- **Amounts are signed exactly as typed.** The CLI and the desktop wallet converted amounts through
  a floating-point number and cut off the rest: `helix tx send <address> 2.01` signed 2.009999999
  HLX. Both now read the digits — `.` or `,` as separator, up to nine decimals — and refuse
  anything else (`1e3`, a tenth decimal, a minus sign) before anything is signed (#257).
- **`helix tx send --memo <text>`** carries a note in the transfer, up to 256 bytes of UTF-8 — how an
  exchange that receives on one address tells deposits apart. `helix tx status` shows it (#258).
- **Signing on a machine that is never online:** `helix tx send … --offline --nonce <n> --fee
  <nano>` signs without asking any node and prints the signed transaction; `helix tx submit <file>`
  (or `-` for stdin) sends it from an online machine. The transaction id is printed at signing
  (#258).
- **`helix chain status` shows the base fee and the chain id** — the two values offline signing
  needs.

**API**

- **Every amount also as an exact decimal string in nano-HLX:** `balance_nano`, `staked_nano`,
  `unbonding_stake_nano`, `circulating_supply_nano`, `total_burned_nano`, `amount_nano`,
  `fee_nano`. The `…_hlx` fields stay, for display — a double cannot hold every nano-HLX amount
  (#256).
- **A transfer's `memo`** in every transaction view, and in `GET /transactions/:hash` also
  `fee_burned_nano`, `fee_to_validator_nano` and the raw `data_hex` (#256).

**Docs:** a new page, [Integrating Helix](https://github.com/silvra-net/helix/blob/master/docs/exchange-integration.md),
for exchanges and custodians — deposits, withdrawals, nonces, and what each answer means.
